blocks.text: A masonry pier under a lintel is loaded slightly off its centreline by the beam that rests on it. A pier that seems to be in comfortable compression can still develop a crack on one face, because the small offset adds a bending stress that is large enough to cancel the compression. The same idea governs hooks, clamps and brackets whose load line is offset from the member's axis.

blocks.markdown: When a member carries an axial force $P$ and a bending moment $M$ at the same time, and the response is linear elastic, the stresses simply **add** (superposition). The axial force gives a uniform direct stress $\sigma_0=P/A$; the moment gives a linearly varying bending stress $\sigma_b=My/I$. If the axial force acts parallel to the axis but at a distance $e$ from the centroid (an **eccentric** load), it is statically equivalent to the same force through the centroid plus a moment $M=Pe$.

blocks.title: Eccentric loading
blocks.text: A load $P$ applied at eccentricity $e$ from the centroidal axis produces the same internal effects as a centric force $P$ and a moment $M=Pe$. The stress at a point at distance $y$ from the neutral (centroidal) axis is $\sigma=\dfrac{P}{A}\pm\dfrac{M\,y}{I}$, with signs fixed by whether each effect is tensile or compressive at that point.

blocks.caption: Rectangle $b\times h$ with the load offset $e$ along the depth $h$; compression taken as negative in the worked example below.

blocks.title: Short rectangular column with eccentric compression
blocks.prompt: A short column is 200 mm wide and 300 mm deep. A compressive load of 360 kN acts parallel to the axis at 40 mm from the centroid, along the 300 mm direction. Find the stresses at the two edges.

steps.text: Moment and section modulus about the axis parallel to the 200 mm side.
Bending stress magnitude at the edges.
Combine: the edge nearer the load adds, the far edge subtracts.

blocks.answer: The near edge carries 10.8 MPa compression and the far edge 1.2 MPa compression: the whole section is still in compression.

blocks.markdown: **The core (kern) of a section.** If the load is moved further from the centroid, the far-edge stress $-\sigma_0+\sigma_b$ eventually becomes zero and then tensile. For a rectangle the far-edge stress is $-\frac{P}{bh}\left(1-\frac{6e}{h}\right)$, which is zero when $e=h/6$. Loads within the middle third of the depth keep the whole section in compression; this region is the **core** or kernel of the section. Materials such as masonry or unreinforced concrete, which cannot take tension, must be loaded inside the core.

headers: Limit of eccentricity for no tension
rows: tension appears at the far edge
blocks.caption: The core of common sections

blocks.title: Eccentricity beyond the core
blocks.prompt: The same column (200 x 300 mm, P = 360 kN compression) is loaded at 75 mm eccentricity along the 300 mm side. Find the edge stresses and say whether tension occurs.

steps.text: Limit for no tension: h/6 = 50 mm. The offset 75 mm is larger, so tension is expected.
Combine with the 6.0 MPa direct compression.

blocks.answer: The far edge is in 3.0 MPa tension (a masonry column would crack there) and the near edge carries 15.0 MPa compression.

blocks.title: Offset load on a bracket
blocks.prompt: A steel bracket bar has a rectangular section 20 mm thick and 60 mm deep. It carries a tensile pull of 12 kN whose line of action lies 40 mm from the centroidal axis, on side A of the 60 mm depth. Find the stress at the edge on side A and the opposite edge B.

steps.text: Bending stress magnitude is 40 MPa, tensile on side A (where the pull is applied) and compressive on side B.

blocks.answer: Edge A is in 50 MPa tension and edge B in 30 MPa compression; the offset multiplies the nominal stress by five.

blocks.title: Check the sign at each point
blocks.text: Decide for each effect whether it is tension or compression at the point you are examining. Bending stress uses $I$ and $y$ about the axis the moment turns about. The superposition holds only for linear elastic behaviour and short members (long slender columns also bend more under load, which is not covered here).

points: An eccentric axial load P at offset e is equivalent to a central load plus a moment M = Pe; direct and bending stresses add by superposition.
Stress at a point is P/A plus or minus M y/I, with the sign set by whether each effect is tensile or compressive there.
For a rectangle, tension first appears when e exceeds h/6 (the middle-third rule); the core of a circle has e = d/8.

questions.stem: A short member carries an axial force P and a bending moment M. The normal stress at a point a distance y from the neutral axis is:

options.text: P/A only, since bending adds no normal stress
P/A plus or minus M y/I

questions.correctOptionText: P/A plus or minus M y/I

distractorRationale.c: Correct: superposition of direct and bending stress.

questions.explanation: For linear elastic behaviour the direct stress P/A is uniform and the bending stress My/I varies linearly. The total stress at a point is their algebraic sum.

questions.stem: For a rectangular column of depth h, a compressive load applied within the middle third of the depth (at e less than h/6) results in:

distractorRationale.a: Correct: for e < h/6, P/A exceeds Pe/S.
distractorRationale.c: Stress at the centroid is P/A, not zero, as bending contributes nothing there.
distractorRationale.d: Eccentric load makes the stress non-uniform.

questions.explanation: The far-edge stress is -(P/A)(1 - 6e/h), which is still compressive when 6e/h < 1. The middle-third rule follows directly.

questions.stem: An eccentric tensile load P is applied to a bar at offset e. Which description is statically equivalent?

options.text: A load P through the centroid plus a moment P/e
A load Pe through the centroid
A load P at the centroid with no moment
A load P through the centroid plus a moment Pe

questions.correctOptionText: A load P through the centroid plus a moment Pe

distractorRationale.a: The moment is the product, not the quotient.
distractorRationale.b: A force cannot be multiplied by a distance.
distractorRationale.c: Omits the couple produced by moving the load line.
distractorRationale.d: Correct: moving a force parallel to itself adds a couple Pe.

questions.explanation: Shifting a force P by a perpendicular distance e to the centroid requires adding a couple of moment Pe to keep the same effect on the member.

questions.stem: A short column carries a fixed compressive load whose eccentricity is steadily increased (still within the core). What happens to the stress at the edge nearer to the load?

distractorRationale.a: The bending stress at the near edge adds to, not reduces, the compression.
distractorRationale.b: Correct: bending adds to the direct compression there.
distractorRationale.c: Bending stress is proportional to e.
distractorRationale.d: Tension appears only on the far edge, and only beyond the core.

questions.explanation: At the near edge the direct stress and the bending stress are both compressive, so increasing e raises the compressive stress. At the far edge the bending stress is tensile and reduces the compression.

questions.stem: True or false: the core of a solid circular section of diameter d extends to an eccentricity of d/8 from the centroid.
questions.explanation: Setting P/A = P e c/I for a circle gives e = d/8. Loads inside this circle of diameter d/4 leave the whole section in compression.

questions.stem: A short column is 150 mm wide and 250 mm deep and carries a compressive load of 300 kN acting 30 mm from the centroid along the 250 mm direction. Find the magnitude of the maximum compressive stress in MPa.

A rectangular masonry pier that cannot resist tension has a depth of 240 mm in the direction of load eccentricity. What is the largest eccentricity of a compressive load for which no tension occurs, in mm?
questions.explanation: Tension first appears at e = h/6 = 240/6 = 40 mm. Loads within the middle third of the depth keep the section in compression.

questions.stem: A circular steel bar of diameter 30 mm supports a tensile load of 15 kN whose line of action is 25 mm from the bar's axis. Find the maximum tensile stress in the bar in MPa (use S = pi d^3/32).
questions.explanation: A = 706.9 mm^2 gives 21.2 MPa direct. S = pi(30)^3/32 = 2651 mm^3 and M = 15 000 x 25 = 375 000 N mm, so bending = 141.5 MPa. The maximum is 21.2 + 141.5 = 162.7 MPa.

questions.stem: Explain how to find the stress at a corner of a rectangular section loaded by an axial force that acts off-centre in both directions, and why superposition is valid.
markingGuide: Replaces the load by a central force plus moments Pe_x and Pe_y
Bending stress about each axis = M y/I (Mx y/Ix and My x/Iy) with signs for the corner
Algebraically adds the three stress contributions at the corner
Superposition is valid for linear elastic behaviour and small deformations
questions.explanation: Each effect is evaluated as if it acted alone and then summed. Linear elasticity guarantees the effects are independent.

questions.stem: Derive the middle-third rule for a rectangular column, and explain why it matters for a column made of material that cannot carry tension.
markingGuide: States far-edge stress = -P/A + P e/S with S = b h^2/6
Sets it to zero to find e = h/6
States loads inside the middle third keep the whole section in compression
Explains masonry or unreinforced concrete would crack in tension, so the load must lie in the core
questions.explanation: The limit comes from equating the bending stress to the direct stress at the extreme fibre. Brittle materials with negligible tensile strength must be loaded inside this core.
